tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). # Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## Local Chrome

The default daemon can keep many tabs and visit many sites; browser-use has
no per-site, screenshot, or result-count limit that requires a new daemon.

## XcodeBuildMCP
XcodeBuildMCP provides comprehensive tooling for Apple platform development (iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, visionOS).

Prefer XcodeBuildMCP tools over shell commands for Apple platform tasks when available.

Capabilities:
- Session defaults: Configure project, scheme, simulator, and device defaults to avoid repetitive parameters
- Project discovery: Find Xcode projects/workspaces, list schemes, inspect build settings
- Simulator workflows: Build, run, test, install, and launch apps on iOS simulators; manage simulator state (boot, erase, location, appearance)
- Device workflows: Build, test, install, and launch apps on physical devices with code signing
- macOS workflows: Build, run, and test macOS applications
- Log capture: Stream and capture logs from simulators and devices
- LLDB debugging: Attach debugger, set breakpoints, inspect stack traces and variables, execute LLDB commands
- UI automation: Capture screenshots, inspect runtime UI snapshots, perform taps/swipes/gestures, type text, press hardware buttons, and batch multiple same-screen elementRef taps
- SwiftPM: Build, run, test, and manage Swift Package Manager projects
- Project scaffolding: Generate new iOS/macOS project templates

Only simulator workflow tools are enabled by default. If capabilities like device, macOS, debugging, or UI automation are not available, the user must configure XcodeBuildMCP to enable them. See https://xcodebuildmcp.com/docs/configuration for workflow configuration.

Simulator run flow:
- Before your first build, run, or test call in a session, you MUST call session_show_defaults to verify the active project/workspace, scheme, and simulator. Do not assume defaults are configured. Only skip this if you have already called session_show_defaults earlier in the current session.
- If session_show_defaults confirms project/workspace + scheme + simulator are set, call build_run_sim immediately (often with empty arguments).
- Use discover_projs only when session_show_defaults shows project/workspace is missing or wrong.
- Never call discover_projs speculatively or in parallel with session_show_defaults.
- Do not call boot_sim or open_sim as prerequisites for build_run_sim; build_run_sim boots and opens the simulator frontend as needed.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon

  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.

# Alloq implementation

Alloq is a Reflex 0.10 app for resource and project planning. The generic skills
explain Python, Reflex and appkit in general. This skill is the Alloq layer: where
code goes in this repo, which guards it must keep green, and how Alloq tests look.
When the two disagree, this skill wins, because it describes the code as it is.

Stack: Python 3.14, uv workspace (`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac`), Reflex 0.10,
appkit-* (`appkit_mantine as mn`, `appkit_commons`, `appkit_user`, `appkit_ui`),
SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, Pydantic, Alembic, PostgreSQL in production and SQLite in tests.
UI text is German. Code, comments and log messages are English.

## Workflow for every task

1. **Search memory** for the feature words and for error text you see. Past sessions
   stored traps here (for example the mixin rule and the umlaut escaping in tests).
2. **Read the reference code of the layer you touch** before writing. The canonical
   slice is departments (see the architecture map). Copying its shape is faster and
   keeps reviews short.
3. **Plan the smallest diff.** Change the layers the task needs and nothing else. Do
   not move files, rename folders or refactor neighbours unless asked.
4. **Write or adjust the test first**, in the test file of the package you change.
   For a bug, first write a test that fails because of the bug. Run the touched test
   files once before changing code, so you know which failures were already there;
   report those instead of fixing them inside the same diff.
5. **Implement.**
6. **Run the gates**: `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test`.
   For a quick loop run only the touched test files with
   `uv run pytest <file> -q`, but run `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` whenever
   you add or change an event handler.
7. **Check file sizes**: `python .claude/skills/alloq-implementation/scripts/check_file_sizes.py`.
8. **Update memory** with any new trap or decision that the code itself does not show.

## Architecture map

Host app `app/` (entry `app/app.py`, admin pages `app/pages/*.py`, sidebar in
`app/components/sidebar.py`) plus uv workspace packages in `components/`:

| Package | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `alloq-commons` | shared kernel: entities, models, repositories, shared services, shared UI, `theme.py`, `roles.py`, `access.py` |
| `alloq-project` | projects and planning: `components/`, `services/`, `states/`, `pages.py` |
| `alloq-dashboard` | dashboard and portfolio: same layout, `models.py` for card payloads |
| `alloq-team` | team overview and employees: same layout |

Layers, in the order data flows (paths for departments under
`components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/`):

| Layer | Where | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity | `entities/department.py` | `class XEntity(Entity, Base)`, `to_dict()` with every field |
| Model | `models/department.py` | Pydantic read model plus `XCreate` write model with `Field` limits |
| Repository | `repositories/department_repository.py` | `BaseRepository[XEntity, AsyncSession]`, `model_class`, module singleton `x_repo` |
| Service | `<pkg>/services/*.py` | pure functions and dataclasses; DB loading kept in `*_inputs.py` or loader functions |
| State | `state/department_states.py` | `rx.State`, `rx.Field` vars, `@rx.event` handlers |
| Component | `components/department.py` | plain functions returning `rx.Component`, built from `mn.*` and shared parts |
| Page | `app/pages/departments.py` or `<pkg>/pages.py` | page factory `create_x_page(sidebar, route, title)` using `app_page` |
| Registration | `app/app.py` | call the factory with `sidebar()`; add a sidebar entry if needed |
| Migration | `alembic/versions/YYYY_MM_DD_<topic>.py` | hand-written, real `downgrade()` |

Dependency direction: feature packages import `alloq_commons` and appkit, never
`app` (`tests/test_component_boundaries.py` fails otherwise). Feature packages do not
import each other unless that import already exists. `app` may import everything.

`alloq_commons` has both `state/` (departments, roles) and `states/` (holidays). Put
new code next to its closest neighbour and do not merge the folders unasked.

Details, snippets and the background-load pattern: `references/architecture.md`.

## Where does this code belong?

- **Pure calculation** (scores, sums, sorting, grouping, labels) goes into a service
  function or a small dataclass, testable without a database. Examples:
  `alloq_dashboard/services/resource_path.py`, `alloq_project/services/project_sorting.py`.
- **Database reads and writes** go through a repository method, or a loader function
  such as `load_departments()` or `portfolio_inputs.py`. States do not build SQL.
- **UI state** (open dialogs, filters, toggles, selection) lives in the state. When the
  state file is large, put new vars and handlers into a mixin
  (`class XListState(rx.State, mixin=True)`), never into a substate; substates break
  tests that create the state on its own.
- **Rendering** goes into function components that read state vars. No logic beyond
  `rx.cond` / `rx.foreach` and formatting.
- **A value both the UI and a test need** (labels, messages, column lists) becomes a
  module constant, so tests can assert on it.

## Security: the handler authorization contract

Access levels (`alloq_commons.access`): admins may do everything; the project
manager role may read and edit every planning page (dashboard, planning, projects,
team) but not the administration; the employee role may only read planning and
projects. Page guards (`admin_only=True`, `editor_only`, `viewer_only`) only hide
the page. Event handlers run over the websocket for anyone with a session, so every
handler protects itself. `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` enforces this for all
states in the four packages. For each new or changed handler pick exactly one case:

1. **Reads or writes data in a planning package** (`alloq_dashboard`,
   `alloq_project`, `alloq_team`, `SidebarState`) → `@rx.event` then
   `@requires_editor` from `alloq_commons.access`. This is the default; the guard
   test rejects `@requires_admin` there.
1b. **Administration state** (`DepartmentState`, `RoleState`, `HolidayState`,
   `DatabaseAccessState`, listed in `ADMIN_STATES`) → `@requires_admin` from
   `appkit_user.authentication.decorators`.
2. **Read-only load the employee role may also run** → `@requires_viewer` from
   `alloq_commons.access`, and add the name to `VIEWER_HANDLERS`. It must not write.
3. **Only changes UI state** (open/close, set filter, toggle) → no decorator, add the
   name to `UI_ONLY_HANDLERS["<ConcreteState>"]`. The test scans its source and the
   `self.` helpers it calls for DB markers (`get_asyncdb_session`, `_repo.`,
   `aggregation.`, ...), so a UI-only handler must not touch a repository or session.
4. **Background handler** (`@rx.event(background=True)`) → guard decorators are not
   allowed (they need the state lock). Check edit rights inside `async with self`
   through `_CardLoadMixin._run_card_load` (`_can_edit`) and list it in
   `INLINE_ADMIN_CHECK`.

Edit controls in the planning UI go inside `editor_only(...)` or use
`disabled=~CAN_EDIT`; `admin_only(...)` is for administration only.

Handlers defined in a mixin are listed under the concrete state that mixes it in
(`TeamState`, `ProjectState`, `PlanningStore`), because the test skips mixins.
Remove allowlist entries when you delete or guard a handler; stale entries fail too.
Run the test after every handler change.

## Style that ruff does not catch

- German UI strings, including toasts: `rx.toast.error("Fehler beim Erstellen der
  Abteilung.", position="top-right")`. English for code, comments, docstrings, logs.
- `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` per module; `%s` arguments, never f-strings
  in log calls; `logger.exception(...)` in the final `except Exception` of a handler.
- Handler error shape: `ValidationError` → German hint, `IntegrityError` → duplicate
  message, `Exception` → `logger.exception` plus a generic German error toast.
- Colors, radii and shadows only from `alloq_commons.theme` (`theme.CARD`,
  `theme.TEXT_MUTED`, `theme.BLUE[6]`, ...). The theme is macOS blue; ignore the old
  teal design artifact.
- Use `mn.*` components. Load `appkit-mantine-reference` before using one you have
  not used in this task; its props are not in your training data.
- HTML attributes on `mn` inputs: `max_length=20` turns into CSS and limits nothing.
  Use `custom_attrs={"maxLength": 20}` for the browser limit, and keep the real check
  in the write model (`Field(max_length=20)`).
- State vars: `name: rx.Field[T] = rx.field(default)`; lists use
  `rx.field(default_factory=list)`. Type hints on every function, including tests.
- Prefer shared parts over new ones: `modal_form_layout`, `modal_footer`,
  `delete_dialog`, `toolbar_search`, `primary_button`, `section`, `app_page`,
  `window_toolbar`, `de_number`.

## Testing standards

Coverage must stay at 80 % or more (branch coverage, `fail_under = 80`). Put tests in
the package that owns the code: `components/<pkg>/tests/test_<feature>.py`. App-level
tests and the guards live in `tests/`.

- **Entity/model**: `to_dict()` keys, `XCreate` rejects bad input.
- **Service**: plain unit tests with hand-built inputs, no mocks needed.
- **State**: create the state directly, patch `MODULE.x_repo` and
  `MODULE.get_asyncdb_session`, fake the admin with `_as_admin`, and drive handlers
  with `_run`, which returns the toast text. Copy the helpers from
  `components/alloq-commons/tests/test_departments.py`.
- **Component**: render with `str(component())` and assert on var names or module
  constants. `str()` escapes umlauts (`ä` becomes `\u00e4`), so assert on the constant.
- **Migration with data changes**: add a test in `tests/test_migrations.py` that runs
  the migration offline on SQLite.

Recipes and snippets: `references/testing.md`.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Test written first; new behaviour and the bug case are covered
- [ ] `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` all green
- [ ] `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` and `tests/test_component_boundaries.py` green
- [ ] Every new handler has its guard or its allowlist entry
- [ ] New migration is hand-written, uses `op.batch_alter_table` for column changes,
      has a real `downgrade()`, and its revision is added to `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in
      `app/desktop/schema.py`
- [ ] No touched file grew past 1000 lines; files already over it did not grow
      without reason (see `references/pitfalls.md`)
- [ ] German UI text, theme tokens, no `print`, no f-strings in logs
- [ ] Memory updated with new traps or decisions

Per change type (new field, new handler, new page, new service, bug fix):
`references/checklists.md`. Known traps: `references/pitfalls.md`.

## Which generic skill for what

| Need | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| Python style, logging, typing, design patterns | `python-coding`, `python-clean-code` |
| Reflex state design, events, background tasks | `reflex-state-and-architecture`, `reflex-docs` |
| Writing state tests in general | `reflex-testing-state` |
| Config, service registry, repositories, column types | `appkit-commons` |
| Any `mn.*` component or prop | `appkit-mantine-reference` |
| Shrinking a big file you touched | `code-cleanup` |

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

"""Editor of the selected story in the side column."""

from typing import Any

import reflex as rx
from alloq_commons import theme
from alloq_commons.components.list_view import inspector, inspector_section

import appkit_mantine as mn
from alloq_offer.workshop.states.map_proposal_state import MapProposalState
from alloq_offer.workshop.states.map_state import SENTENCE_HINT, MapState

DRAWER_LABEL = "Story bearbeiten"
SPLIT = "Aufteilen"
SPLIT_AI = "KI-Aufteilung vorschlagen"
ARCHIVE = "Archivieren"
CLOSE = "Schließen"
SAVE = "Speichern"
TITLE_LABEL = "Titel"
DESCRIPTION_LABEL = "Beschreibung"
DESCRIPTION_PLACEHOLDER = "Hintergrund, Hinweise, offene Fragen"
ORIGIN_TITLE = "Herkunft"
WRAPPED_FIELDS = frozenset({"benefit"})
"""Story parts shown as growing text areas; line breaks become spaces on save."""
FIELDS = (
    ("role", "Als", "Rolle"),
    ("goal", "möchte ich", "Ziel oder Handlung"),
    ("benefit", "um", "Nutzen"),
)


def _field(name: str, label: str, placeholder: str) -> rx.Component:
    story = MapState.selected
    if name in WRAPPED_FIELDS:
        return mn.textarea(
            label=label,
            placeholder=placeholder,
            name=name,
            default_value=story[name].to(str),
            autosize=True,
            min_rows=2,
            custom_attrs={"maxLength": 300},
        )
    return mn.text_input(
        label=label,
        placeholder=placeholder,
        name=name,
        default_value=story[name].to(str),
        custom_attrs={"maxLength": 300},
    )


def _icon(icon: str, label: str, **props: Any) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.action_icon(
        rx.icon(icon, size=16),
        variant="subtle",
        size="md",
        aria_label=label,
        custom_attrs={"title": label},
        **props,
    )


def _header() -> rx.Component:
    """Key, editable title and the actions; stays on top while the body scrolls."""
    story = MapState.selected
    return mn.box(
        mn.group(
            mn.text(
                story["key"].to(str), fz="11.5px", c=theme.TEXT_MUTED, ff="monospace"
            ),
            mn.group(
                _icon("save", SAVE, color="blue", type="submit"),
                _icon(
                    "archive", ARCHIVE, color="red", on_click=MapState.archive_selected
                ),
                _icon("x", CLOSE, color="gray", on_click=MapState.close_story),
                gap=2,
                wrap="nowrap",
            ),
            justify="space-between",
            wrap="nowrap",
        ),
        mn.textarea(
            name="title",
            default_value=story["title"].to(str),
            variant="unstyled",
            autosize=True,
            min_rows=2,
            custom_attrs={
                "maxLength": 300,
                "aria-label": TITLE_LABEL,
                "title": story["title"].to(str),
            },
            class_name="aq-map-title aq-story-title",
        ),
        class_name="aq-insp-head",
    )


def _place(label: str, options: Any, value: Any, name: str) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.select(
        label=label,
        data=options,
        value=value,
        allow_deselect=False,
        size="sm",
        on_change=lambda picked: (  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
            MapState.place_story(picked, MapState.selected["slice_id"].to(str))
            if name == "task"
            else MapState.place_story(MapState.selected["task_id"].to(str), picked)
        ),
    )


def story_drawer() -> rx.Component:
    story = MapState.selected
    return inspector(
        rx.form(
            _header(),
            _body(story),
            on_submit=MapState.save_story,
            # A new story or revision resets the uncontrolled fields.
            key=story["key"].to(str) + "-" + MapState.revision.to(str),
            class_name="aq-insp-form",
        ),
        label=DRAWER_LABEL,
    )


def _body(story: Any) -> rx.Component:
    return rx.fragment(
        inspector_section(
            "User Story",
            *(_field(*field) for field in FIELDS),
            mn.text(SENTENCE_HINT, fz="12px", c=theme.TEXT_MUTED),
            mn.textarea(
                name="description",
                label=DESCRIPTION_LABEL,
                placeholder=DESCRIPTION_PLACEHOLDER,
                default_value=story["description"].to(str),
                autosize=True,
                min_rows=3,
                max_rows=12,
                custom_attrs={"maxLength": 4000},
            ),
        ),
        inspector_section(
            "Einordnung",
            _place(
                "Aktivität und Aufgabe",
                MapState.task_options,
                story["task_id"].to(str),
                "task",
            ),
            _place(
                "Umsetzungsschnitt",
                MapState.slice_options,
                story["slice_id"].to(str),
                "slice",
            ),
        ),
        inspector_section(
            ORIGIN_TITLE,
            mn.text(story["origin"].to(str) + " · " + story["refs"].to(str), fz="13px"),
        ),
        mn.group(
            mn.button(
                SPLIT, variant="default", size="xs", on_click=MapState.split_selected
            ),
            mn.button(
                SPLIT_AI,
                variant="default",
                size="xs",
                on_click=MapProposalState.propose_split,
            ),
            gap=8,
            wrap="nowrap",
            class_name="aq-insp-foot",
        ),
    )
